details:
ASTRA Health (Astronaut Health Monitoring System) is a software prototype designed to support astronaut health monitoring during long-duration and deep-space missions.

The system collects and visualizes biometric indicators such as heart rate, blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂), blood pressure, skin temperature and sleep-related data. It analyzes incoming measurements to identify unusual patterns and generate alerts. Its proposed architecture includes local data processing and autonomous anomaly detection, allowing astronauts to receive preliminary health information even when communication with Earth is delayed or unavailable. Relevant information could later be transmitted to mission control through a telemetry system.

ASTRA Health aims to improve health awareness, support faster responses to potential medical concerns and contribute to safer future space exploration. Its main benefit is combining biometric monitoring, local analysis and decision support in one accessible interface.

The prototype is developed using HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with a browser-based dashboard, simulated biometric readings, data visualizations and scenario-based alerts. GitHub is used for version control, and Vercel is planned for hosting.

Our creative approach is to consider astronaut health monitoring not simply as data collection, but as an autonomous system capable of interpreting information when immediate assistance from Earth may not be available.

During development, we considered scientific accuracy, limited communication in deep space, usability, data reliability and the distinction between simulated and real measurements. ASTRA Health is currently a prototype, not a clinically validated medical device, and does not use live astronaut sensor data.
